verdict.rationale: Orama documents on-premise support for Orama Cloud, letting you deploy the context server on your own infrastructure, and offers an open-source library whose APIs are designed to stay close to Cloud's. Parity with the hosted product is not shown: the open-source AnswerSession depends on Orama Cloud's Secure Proxy, and on-prem appears to be an engineer-assisted engagement rather than a documented self-serve deployment. Missing for 10: documented feature parity between self-hosted and hosted (e.g. MCP server, managed embeddings), self-serve deployment and operations docs, independent or hands-on corroboration of a self-hosted deployment.

support.subject: As a platform-engineer, I can self-host the full engine — same features as the hosted product — on my own infrastructure

citations.quote: We offer on-premise support for Orama Cloud, allowing you to deploy the context server on your own infrastructure.
It runs in your cloud, on-prem, or dedicated, and our forward-deployed engineers run it with your team.
The APIs are designed to be as close as possible to the **Orama Cloud** APIs, so you can easily migrate your projects from **Orama Cloud** to **Orama Open Source** and vice-versa.
